subject: Novus MSA redline: technical witness / attestation for IP indemnity
content:
From: Ethan Brooks <ethan.brooks@novushealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sarah Li <sarah.li@novushealth.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Redline: MSA + Order Form — IP indemnity & witness request

Ben,

Thanks for the redline. Two items are material blockers for Procurement: the indemnity carve (third-party IP) and an additional ask from our legal team. They want a commitment that, in the event of an infringement claim, Redwood will provide a factual technical declaration (a "technical witness" or "technical attestation") describing how the model produced the alleged output, the model/weights used, and a factual statement of Redwood's access/role — essentially an engineer-signed attestation to help us triage and, if necessary, support a defense.

We attached our annotated MSA and a one-page procurement timeline. Can Redwood provide either:

- a) a firm commitment in the MSA to produce a technical attestation within X business days of notice, or
- b) a binding process (MAP) that lays out the evidence handoff, who signs the attestation, and timelines (our preference).

Procurement has requested a response by EOD 2027-05-05 since they hope to close this week.

Attachments: Novus_MSA_redline.pdf (redline)

Thanks,
Ethan Brooks
Senior Counsel, Novus Health
ethan.brooks@novushealth.com

On Mon, Apr 26, 2027 at 09:20 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com> wrote:

Hi Ethan / Ben / team,

Thanks for flagging. We reviewed Novus's redline and Procurement ask. High-level position from Legal: Redwood will commit to a process to provide technical attestation materials prepared by our engineering team, subject to the limitations below. We do not provide legal opinions as to infringement, but we can provide a factual, time-stamped statement from an engineer that includes:

- model identifier and version used (to the extent determinable)
- runtime environment and prompt/inputs supplied by the customer (if available)
- sequence of events/call logs showing model invocation(s) tied to timestamps
- a factual description of outputs generated and any system-level modifications or fine-tuning performed by Redwood on behalf of the customer

Limitations / guardrails we should include in the MSA / Order Form redline:
- The attestation is limited to factual statements and may not be used as a legal admission.
- Redwood's obligation to prepare the attestation is triggered by (i) receipt of a timely indemnity notice that meets the MSA notice requirements, and (ii) a signed NDA / protective order covering shared technical materials if Novus requests privileged material.
- Response SLA: we can commit to delivery of a draft technical attestation within 15 business days after receiving complete claim materials and evidence from Novus; finalization may require iterative Q&A with Novus and counsel.
- Cost allocation: if the request requires extraordinary engineering time (>8 engineer-hours), parties will negotiate a good-faith cost share or Novus will reimburse reasonable external costs.

I've attached a redline suggestion that inserts a "Technical Attestation" subsection under Section 9 (Indemnification / Cooperation). Please review and tell us what you prefer for SLA and cost terms.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

On Mon, Apr 26, 2027 at 11:05 AM Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com> wrote:

Team — quick operational note from engineering standpoint. We can produce a factual document signed by an engineer, but two practical points:

1) What Novus calls a "technical witness" should be framed as a technical attestation/factual report. Our engineers are comfortable signing factual statements (logs, model id, what was run) but they are not legal witnesses and cannot opine on liability or infringement.

2) To prepare the attestation we will need:
   - Clear claim details (example prompt/seed input, timestamps, evidence of alleged infringing content)
   - Access to the customer's call logs / order form that tie the execution to the alleged output (we can often provide logs if the customer supplied the prompt; if Redwood generated content during a managed workflow we can supply internal traceability)

3) Proposed internal workflow:
   - Legal triage (Kim) receives notice -> opens Legal ticket (LEGAL-332) -> Procurement & CS notified
   - Engineering intake: SRE/ML Eng runs reproducibility check, collects logs, drafts technical attestation (3-10 business days depending on complexity)
   - Attestation reviewed by Legal for privilege/redaction -> delivered to customer under protective order if requested

I've attached a short template (tech_attestation_template.docx) that our engineers can use as a starting point. Happy to walk Novus's counsel through the template if that helps accelerate.

-Mina
Mina Haddad
Head, Applied ML | Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com
Attachment: tech_attestation_template.docx

Ethan —

Appreciate the dialog. Attached is a consolidated response and a tightened SLA. Key points:

- Redwood will include a "Technical Attestation" clause in the MSA: Redwood will provide a factual technical attestation prepared by qualified engineering personnel that describes (i) the model identifier/version; (ii) the runtime environment; (iii) call logs and timestamps linked to the asserted output (to the extent available); and (iv) a factual description of any customization or fine-tuning performed. The attestation will not constitute a legal admission or opinion.

- Triggering & SLAs: obligation triggered upon receipt of a timely indemnity notice with supporting materials. Redwood will deliver a draft attestation within 10 business days of receiving complete claim materials and any necessary access/records from Novus.

- Privilege & protective measures: if privileged materials are required to compose the attestation, parties will execute an appropriate protective order or NDA before production; Redwood reserves the right to redact privileged internal analysis.

- Cost allocation: Redwood will absorb routine preparation costs (up to 8 engineer-hours). If the request requires more than 8 engineer-hours, parties will negotiate a reasonable cost-share or Novus will reimburse additional time at Redwood's standard hourly rate.

Attached: tech_attestation_template.docx (final draft), redline_suggestion.pdf (MSA insertion), procurement_track.pdf (timeline).

Please confirm this meets Novus's needs and whether Procurement can proceed to signature by 2027-05-05. If so, we will circulate a DocuSign with redlines accepted.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
